## Step 1 reading — every queue root of 2026-11-01..07 (Wanted 1, Wanted 2 proposals)

⛔ Reading only, no code. Tree: `objectstack-ai/objectstack` @ `a3ac7fb3` (origin/main). Data: Actions REST, every `CI` and `Lint` `merge_group` run created 2026-10-31..11-07 (3,978 runs; 1,840 builds of each workflow inside the window, as the card measured), the failed jobs, their annotations and logs for every red build, the last `pull_request` run of each root PR before its enqueue, and the `main` push runs at each root's base. Method as the card states it: "a queue build's commit has one parent, the previous group head. Parent is a `main` push or a green group ⇒ root. Parent's `CI` or `Lint` is red ⇒ cascade." Parents are read from the queue branch name (`gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-N-PARENT`); 5 spot-checked against `GET /commits/SHA` → `parents` (`7db85179`, `37f60419`, `18aca111`, `03ba1ce9`, `2f48926c`): one parent each, all 5 equal to the branch name's.

Classes, quoted from the card: "(a) stale base: the PR's last green run was N merges behind `main` when it was enqueued; (b) not selected on the PR: the gate is narrowed on `pull_request` (path scoping or dispatch-gates) and full in the queue — the #31512 shape; (c) flake: green on rerun with the same tree; (d) interaction between queue entries." **K** below = merges on `main` (first-parent) between the diff base of the PR's last CI run (its Test Core `Affected-set diff base` line) and the queue entry's base.

### Counts

| class | roots | cascades behind them | cascades per root |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) stale base | 21 | 122 | 5.8 |
| (b) not selected on the PR | 6 | 23 | 3.8 |
| (c) flake | 36 | 5 | 0.1 |
| (d) entry interaction, genuine | 0 | 0 | — |
| (d\*) transitive: one-hop rule calls it a root | 5 | 7 | 1.4 |
| **total** | **68** | **157** | 2.3 |

225 red builds = 68 + 157. The card's 66 roots + 2 unclassified resolve here as 68 roots: every parent of the 225 is in the run index once 10-31 is included.

### What the table says

1. **Stale base is a third of the roots and four fifths of the cascades.** 21 roots carry 122 of 157 cascades. Families: gate tightened on `main` after the PR's base (alias gate, 5); a locale against labels that landed after it, both directions of the #31512 shape (5); a generated or hand-counted ledger rewritten by two PRs (spec strictness counts 3, dropped-refinements header 1, tenancy census 1); a pin against a sibling feature that landed after the base (Studio 3, `check:spec-symbols` 1); the skills token ratchet (2). Every (a) row with a measured K has K 7 or more (median 25); one has no Test Core run to read K from.
2. **Flakes are half the roots and almost no cascades, and this is structural.** On `merge_group`, Test Core and Test UI select by `git diff base_sha HEAD`, and `base_sha` is the entry directly ahead (`scripts/ci/select-shard-packages.sh`: "`git diff base_sha HEAD` is exactly what this entry adds"). So the entries behind a flaky entry do not run its test and stay green. Families: 5000 ms timeouts 14 (cli `validate-build-gate-parity` 5, qa `external-driver` 4 — budget fix #31284 landed 11-07 22:30Z, `loop-body-iteration` 3 — #31312 landed 11-08 00:49Z, two singles); the 11-03 20-minute checkout timeouts 7 (#22034, PR #31429; e20c60d2 raised the budget to 25 min); Live E2E `studio-customize-journey` 4 (11-05); clock-boundary pins 4 (`organization-access-policy`, fixed by #31213; `mcp-object-schema-mask`, fixed by #31195); `AiChatPage.previewDraft-12968` 2; others 5. 28 of the 36 went green on the next entry with the same PR head. None of the 21 (a) roots did.
3. **(b) is two mechanisms, neither a `pull_request` narrowing in lint.yml.** Dogfood does not run on `pull_request` by design (#30878, #30991). The other 4 roots are `check:liveness` (spec liveness citations into `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`):
   - The PR run of #30716 replayed `@objectstack/spec:test` from the turbo cache (`cache hit, replaying logs 09ab3604…`), because spec's test hash does not cover the objectql files `check-liveness.test.ts` reads. The queue executed it (`cache miss, executing 86ebed7f…`) and went red, twice. The `Spec Liveness Check` workflow did not run on that PR run either, because its `paths:` list only the spec side.
   - #30341's own queue build (`f672e0dc`) also replayed `spec:test` from cache, and its `Spec Liveness Check` `merge_group` run was **red**. That workflow is not a required context, so the entry landed, and `main` stayed red on liveness until #30368 (11-05 08:47Z). #30357 and #30321 paid for it. In the window, 53 queue runs of `Spec Liveness Check` were red, and 4 of those entries landed anyway (#30341, #30353, #30351, #30298).
4. **No genuine (d).** All 5 rows marked (d\*) have a red ancestor 2 to 6 entries up that failed the same test (#29100, #29521, #29623). The green entries between them did not select that test (the `base_sha` mechanism in item 2), so the one-hop rule calls them roots. They disappear with their (a) root. For the 7-day re-reading, I suggest counting a red whose nearest red ancestor failed the same test as a cascade.
5. **Re-enqueued with an unchanged head: 12 roots.** 5 were deterministic reds that went red again: #30716, #30866, #30902 twice and #31233. They cost 28 cascades, 18% of the window. AGENTS.md §7 already says "a stale red clears only with a new commit (`git merge origin/main`), never by re-running". The other 7 were flakes, and re-trying them was correct.

### The 11-06 15:26Z alias-gate root (asked first)

The first alias red, at 15:26:34Z, is a cascade: #30849's entry `37f60419` sat behind #30866's token-ratchet root `7db85179`. All 65 alias reds trace to three PRs whose PR-run base predates #30969 (`acd190b2`, landed 14:55:57Z). #30969 is the source-reach rule that judges the test files a change edits. The three PRs:

- #30849: base `a2f523aa`, K 58. Its last PR run was attempt 2 of a 07:33Z run.
- #30954: base `c1da9571`.
- #30902: base `1aeeafd9`. Its last PR run was created at 15:08Z, after #30969 landed, but it still tested a 14:13Z base: a run that starts after a landing has not necessarily seen it. It was then re-enqueued twice with the same head, `e0985fe`.

Alias reds by root: `18aca111` 13, `37f02a9b` 14, `f8516e4f` 12, `d859d2e9` 9, `d167fcaf` 2, plus 15 in other roots' cascades that already held one of the three (`7db85179` 10, `45b4e886` 4, `2c31cdf4` 1). Total 65.

Lint queue reds by gate over all 225 red builds (`Red gate:` annotations): alias 65, untranslated declared labels 39, app-nav translated 35, skills token ratchet 29, translation bundles 11, tenancy census 6, write-pace self-test 1. The card had 4 for untranslated labels; I count 39.

### Step 1.3 — cheapest fix per class with 3 or more roots

- **(a) stale base: 21 roots, 122 cascades. Lane: the enqueue procedure (`domain:skills`, for the seat to file).** No CI-side fix exists here: a `pull_request` run cannot see a landing that happens after its base. Of the card's two options, a refresh rule keyed on K catches this class:

  | refresh when K is at least | (a) roots caught | (a) cascades caught | other rows also refreshed |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 10 | 19 of 21 | 116 of 122 | 21 of 47 |
  | 15 | 16 of 21 | 108 of 122 | 12 of 47 |
  | 20 | 13 of 21 | 82 of 122 | 10 of 47 |

  At the enqueue, K is `git rev-list --count --first-parent PRBASE..origin/main`, where PRBASE is the diff base of the PR's last green run. I recommend K 15: one extra PR CI round on about a quarter of entries, against 108 of 122 cascades. The second rule, "not re-enqueued until its head changes or the ejection is read as a flake", would have saved 28 more cascades in this window. That half also belongs to the enqueue procedure.
- **(b) not selected: 6 roots, 23 cascades. Lane: CI-side, `domain:devx`, this card. Only the `check:liveness` sub-class (4 roots) is a CI fix; the 2 dogfood roots are the ruled two-speed design.** The cheapest fix reuses the existing 3 s `check:liveness` step and creates no gate. Run `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:liveness` on every `pull_request` and `merge_group` inside a required lane. That means folding its step into a required `lint.yml` lane, so that a red stops the entry instead of riding through as an advisory check. `lint.yml` is inside the Claim's surface; the PR is Tier H and goes in the order the seat chooses after #31429 and #31519. Whether `spec-liveness-check.yml` then retires its now-duplicate step, or keeps its spec-only `paths:`, is outside the Claim's surface, so the seat decides. A second option is for `@objectstack/spec#test` to hash the files its repo-reading tests read; I do not recommend it, because the ledger cites most packages, so every PR would miss the cache on spec tests.
- **(c) flake: 36 roots, 5 cascades. No CI-side fix, and no fix on this card.** The queue already contains flakes (item 2), and the families with 3 or more roots are test fixes for their own lanes. `external-driver` and `loop-body-iteration` already have budget fixes landed (#31284, #31312), the checkout family is #22034 (PR #31429), and the clock pins are fixed (#31213, #31195). Still open: cli `validate-build-gate-parity` (5 roots on 11-02 and 11-06, all one 5000 ms case) and Live E2E `studio-customize-journey` (4 roots on 11-05). Each is one card to its owning lane, if the seat finds no open card.
- **(d\*) transitive: 5 roots, 7 cascades. No fix needed.** They vanish with their (a) root. Change the measurement only, as in item 4.
